paper_metadata.title: Reduction of Qubits in Quantum Algorithm for Monte Carlo Simulation by Pseudo-random Number Generator

summary: This paper proposes a gate-based quantum Monte Carlo method that sequentially generates pseudo-random numbers on a quantum circuit and uses amplitude estimation to estimate sampled averages with O(1/epsilon) oracle complexity versus O(1/epsilon^2) classically. The proof-of-concept simulation uses a 2-variable trigonometric integral with theta = pi/6, Nsamp = 8, a 5-bit LCG (a=11, c=0, m=31, seed=1), and reports 0.078391 versus the exact sampled average 0.078394 and exact integral 0.074578.

experiments.description: Quantum Monte Carlo integration using a pseudo-random number generator on a quantum circuit, demonstrated on a 2-variable trigonometric integral with a small LCG-based PRNG and amplitude estimation on Qiskit.

algorithm.variant: Amplitude estimation applied to Monte Carlo integration with sequential PRNG generation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: 5-bit PRN values from an LCG are used as sampled grid points; the integrand value is encoded into the phase of a single ancilla qubit via sequential Ry rotations controlled by PRN bits.
problem_formulation.objective_function: I = (1/theta^Nvar) * integral_0^theta dx1 ... integral_0^theta dxNvar sin^2(sum_i xi)

problem_instance.description: Proof-of-concept evaluation of a 2-dimensional trigonometric integral on a simulator.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic integral with theta=pi/6 and Nvar=2; PRN sequence generated by LCG with period 30 and 5-bit outputs.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Discretize each variable into 2^r grid points using (x+1/2)/2^r * theta; sample 8 PRN-based points from the LCG sequence.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Simulator-based proof-of-concept; compare exact integral, exact average over sampled points, and quantum estimate.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Generate PRN sequence with LCG; map PRN values to grid points; prepare amplitude-estimation likelihood data from repeated measurements.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Estimate theta_a by maximizing the likelihood function over observed counts; compare estimated integral to exact integral and exact sampled average.

speedup_claims.conditions: for target error epsilon, amplitude estimation gives O(1/epsilon) oracle complexity versus O(1/epsilon^2) classically
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states this as a theoretical complexity result; the simulator demonstration is only a proof-of-concept and does not measure wall-clock speedup.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(N_orac^{-1}) error scaling for amplitude estimation; overall oracle-call complexity for target error epsilon is O(1/epsilon)
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(1/epsilon^2) oracle/sample complexity for classical Monte Carlo
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: 2πd * sqrt(E_samp(1-E_samp)) in the paper's error bound
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_classical: c * sigma_fNran in the paper's error bound

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; only a 2-variable toy integral with Nsamp=8 and a simulator demonstration
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require a fault-tolerant quantum computer with enough qubits for large-scale Monte Carlo and amplitude estimation; the paper does not provide a practical crossover estimate
limiting_factors: Only a proof-of-concept simulator run is reported
No wall-clock quantum-vs-classical benchmark is provided
The claimed speedup is asymptotic O(1/epsilon) vs O(1/epsilon^2), not experimentally demonstrated
Circuit depth grows with the number of random numbers due to sequential PRNG generation
The paper explicitly notes the circuit is too large for current public simulators or machines

notes: The paper explicitly states use of the Qiskit simulator and gives the PRNG size (5-bit output) and sample count, but does not report a total qubit count for the full circuit; num_qubits is therefore not directly reported and is left null in the resource block, with the experiment description inferred from the circuit structure.
Circuit depth is discussed qualitatively (sequential PRNG generation increases depth) but no numeric depth is reported.
Hardware type inferred as simulator_other because the paper says the experiment was performed using the IBM Qiskit simulator and no real QPU is named.
The authors claim quadratic speedup in oracle complexity for Monte Carlo via amplitude estimation, but the only experiment is a small simulator proof-of-concept on a 2-variable integral.
No practical advantage over classical methods is demonstrated.
